findings.title: The unit-5 check runs before the stems and overrides unit 4's keep rule: a body named after a separator in closed-list words is dropped (AwardSummary becomes Placeholder)
findings.scenario:
Context first: I read all 1,316 changed folds in simulation.json and none is a real name (all pointers or form labels), so dry 2283's counts stand. The false drops below are prospective and would hit the fold and the text parser on new notices or a reparse.

`section_reference_pointer` runs before `placeholder_hit` and `pointer_names`, and the grammar ignores separators. So when the body named after `:` or ` - ` is made only of list words, the name stops being AwardSummary and becomes Placeholder.

A temporary probe (integration test, since deleted), run with the gate's flags and package set, EXIT=0:
- `See section VI.2: Avis` gives srp=true, Placeholder.
- `See section VI.2: Point P`, `Voir VI.2 - Point P`, `Voir rubrique VI.2 : Point P` and `Siehe oben (I.1): Point P` all give Placeholder.
- The controls still go through the keep rule: `See section: Avis`, `Siehe oben: Avis`, `Siehe oben: Point P`, `See section VI.2: Colas` and `See section VI.2: Avis Budget` all give AwardSummary.

Before unit 5, `See section VI.2: Avis` went through the same keep rule as `See section: Avis`, so it was AwardSummary. In `drop_decision` that matters a lot: one AwardSummary name keeps the whole party, while a Placeholder party is dropped and gets no guard-3 identifier rescue. So the winner Avis (car rental) or Point P (Saint-Gobain building materials), both frequent French public-contract winners, would lose every role and result even when a SIRET is published.

The doc comments claim the opposite: "every word closed-list, so nothing in it names a body" and "the keep rule reads past them as before". `avis` is a SECTION_NOTICE_WORDS entry; `point` and `p` are SECTION_LOCATORS entries.
findings.fix:
In `reference_shape` (or `section_reference`), read a separator-introduced tail after the last reference the way unit 4's keep rule does. When the raw text after the last reference opens with `:`, ` - `, `–`, `—` or `(`, the words after it may only be FORM_SECTION_TITLES, positions or joiners. Otherwise return None, so the stem path and `pointer_names` decide, which gives AwardSummary for `: Avis` and Placeholder for `: Review Body`.

I re-implemented the grammar in Python and checked it against the simulation: it accepts every one of the 1,316 changed folds and nothing the Rust rule rejects. Under this rule no changed fold goes back to `name` (`Patrz sekcja VI.2) - informacje dodatkowe` and `See section VI.4.1: Review Body` still drop). Add `See section VI.2: Avis` / `Voir VI.2 - Point P` (AwardSummary) to `a_name_beside_a_section_reference_stays_a_name`.

findings.title: The Label shape takes any list word after a reference, so a lot-numbered winner whose company name is list words is dropped (`I.4) Avis`, `I.3) Point P`)
findings.scenario:
`reference_shape` accepts a Label (no pointer word) when every piece is in any closed list. So a reference followed by a Notice, Locator, Noun or Joiner word that is really a company name passes.

The probe returned srp=true and Placeholder for:
- `I.4) Avis` and `I.4) AVIS`: Reference + Notice.
- `I.3) Point P`, `I.3) POINT P` and `I.3) Point.P`: Reference + Locator + Locator.
- `II.1) Le Point`, `I.2) Il Punto`, `I.2) The Point` and `I.2) De Punt`.
- `I.5) Art`, `I.6) Item` and `I.7) Bloc`.
- `Point P (voir I.1)` and `Point P, voir VI.2`: a Locator opens and runs into a pointer.

Meanwhile `I.4) Ricoh` and `I.2) Avis Location` stay names.

The winner-slot shape is real. Dry 2283's non_exact list holds about 50 `I.n) <winner>` spellings that unit 5 rightly keeps (`I.6) Colas`, `I.4) Brake France`, `I.3) Razel RNF`, `III.1) Normandie Motoculture`). A French lot-numbered award to Avis or Point P, published like those, becomes a Placeholder party: no organization is minted, every role and result winner naming it is dropped, there is no identifier guard, and the text parser refuses it on reparse.

The plan has no such spelling today, which I checked by grep (`avis`, `point p`, `le point`), so the current drain is unaffected.
findings.fix:
Tighten the grammar in two places:
- (a) Every Locator must reach a Reference or Number through Locators, Joiners or Titles only, with no pointer, notice word, noun or end of name in between. This rejects `Point P`, `Le Point`, `Item` and `Point P (voir I.1)`, and keeps `Please see the item under section VI.4.2`, `Siehe VI.3) Nr. 1` and `Se reporter à la rubrique IV.3 point 16`.
- (b) In the Label shape, after the last reference allow only titles, positions and joiners. This rejects `I.4) Avis` and keeps `V.1) AWARD AND CONTRACT VALUE:`, `Section VI.4.2) below`, `VI.4.1) i VI.4.2)` and `SECTION VI: OTHER INFORMATION VI.7) Other information: I`.

Cost, measured with the Python re-implementation (which matches the simulation exactly): 3 changed folds / 4 orgs of 19,986 go back to `name`, namely `Please see VI.3 'Additional Information Section'` (2), `See VI.4.1) Review Body Field of this Contract Notice` (1) and `VI.2) tohto oznámenia.` (1). The first two survive if a Locator right after a Title counts as part of that title (`Additional Information Section`, `Review Body Field`).

Add `I.4) Avis`, `I.3) Point P`, `II.1) Le Point` and `Point P (voir I.1)` to the near-miss test.

findings.title: The narrowed echo stops sweeping the Croatian copy, so 24-language TED pointer winners from 2014 on are kept again
findings.scenario:
Unit 5 adds `pointer_led` to `translation_shaped`. A copy is now swept only if it opens with a `SECTION_POINTERS` word (line 1115), and that list has no Croatian word (`vidi`, `vidjeti`). It also has no `odjeljak` locator and no `dodatni podaci` title.

Take an r209 (2014+) EU-institution award. Its winner carries EN `See Section VI.2 'Additional information'.` plus 23 translations, including HR (e.g. `Vidjeti odjeljak VI.2 „Dodatni podaci”.`). The issue's own unit-3 status describes these parties as carrying the pointer "in 24 languages" (604 residual mentions). Croatian is the 24th language, the one 12516947 lacks.

- Unit 4 (deployed): the HR copy is short, has no legal form, carries `vi.2` and a different label. The echo sweeps it and the party drops.

- The unit-4 canary's 12516947 has no HR copy.

The net contract itself still holds. FR/DE template heads are section-reference pointers by themselves. Pointer-led non-template heads are `echo_shaped`.

findings.title: Unit 5 makes every non-English pointer an echo seed, so a bilingual party's named copy now drops with it

findings.title: The `AS` fix in names_a_legal_form has no production effect; the misread list the evidence cites is untouched
findings.scenario: In the fold, names_a_legal_form is reached only through translation_shaped, for a class-None name. A name where `pointer_as` matters (reference_shape Some) is already Placeholder through section_reference, which calls legal_form_reading(raw, true) itself. No list word is a company, Polish or crosswalk form, so the echo never asks, and in the net mentions_by_class short-circuits first. The plumbing therefore only adds a reference_pieces + reference_shape build to every translation_shaped call, and pointer_led builds raw_pieces a second time. findings.fix: Drop `pointer_as` from names_a_legal_form and keep legal_form_reading(raw, true) inside section_reference. Or build the pieces once in translation_shaped and pass them to both checks. To shrink the read list, filter `!ingest::partyname::section_reference_pointer(name)` in supervisor's legal_form list (one line, out of this unit's file scope).

findings.title: section_reference_pointer is about 90% of not_a_name's time for names that carry a section number
findings.scenario: I measured with a temporary probe on the gate's dev profile (debug build; the probe is removed). Times are not_a_name, then section_reference_pointer: `siehe VI.4.1)` 56.6µs, 50.4µs; `Se punkt VI.2) Yderligere oplysninger` 166.8µs, 162.5µs; `V.1) AWARD AND CONTRACT VALUE:` 90µs, 84µs. Without a reference it is 0.1–0.4µs, so the byte pre-check works. Two things drive the cost. `reference_phrase` scans all ~390 phrases of the 8 lists with up to three `split(' ')` passes per phrase, for every piece. `raw_pieces` folds every run (two String allocations each) before the grammar can bail: `Bundesamt für Bauwesen und Raumordnung, Referat II.3` pays 48.6µs and is rejected at its first word. It is bounded and uses no regex, so it is not material next to the fold's DB work. But it runs per party name per notice, and two to four times per org in the walk (net, echo_shaped, then not_a_name again).
findings.fix: Optional: fold pieces lazily and return at the first piece no list holds. Index REFERENCE_LISTS by first word (a sorted static slice with binary search, or pre-split phrases) instead of re-splitting every phrase per piece.
